issues.issue: What standard of review applies to the CTA's interpretation of the interchange and interswitching definitions?
issues.applicant_position: Correctness applies: the issue is jurisdictional and turns on the statutory definitions of interchange and interswitching.
issues.result_quote: The appropriate standard of review is reasonableness.

issues.issue: Is there an interchange at Fort Rouge Yard, given the connecting tracks and storage are 1.9 miles apart?
issues.applicant_position: An interchange needs the connection and storage at the same place; 1.9 miles apart is too far, unlike Celgar.
issues.respondent_position: "Place" is broad; the two elements need not coincide exactly, and the CTA is best placed to define place.
issues.result_quote: These are precisely the kinds of distinctions which the CTA is in the best position to make and it is not for this Court to interfere.

issues.issue: Does BNSF have a line of railway at Fort Rouge Yards through the 1913 Transfer Track Agreement?
issues.applicant_position: The 1913 agreement is only a cost-sharing deal and gives BNSF no interest in CN's land, so BNSF has no line of railway.
issues.respondent_position: The agreement gave BNSF rights to designated land and transfer facilities, enough for a line of railway; the CTA so found.
issues.result_quote: We ought not to substitute our view for the CTA’s in a matter which is so close to its core expertise.

issues.issue: Is CN's status as a local carrier relevant to whether interswitching occurs?
issues.applicant_position: Interswitching requires CN to deliver traffic over its own lines, so CN's use of CP track to reach Patterson defeats it.
issues.respondent_position: Local carrier status matters only for competitive line rates, not interswitching, as the CTA held.
issues.result_quote: I have nothing to add to what the Board said.
